title: Consolidated metering and reconciliation for structured function-call fanout with partial successes
creator: Asha Narayanan
description: Problem: Non-chat endpoints that produce structured output (embeddings + rerank + downstream function/tool invocations) can fan out to multiple backends. We currently: (a) reserve quota when requests enter the system, (b) issue metering events at completion, and (c) run a weekly reconciliation job. This model breaks for partial-success scenarios (some tool invocations succeed, others fail or time out), speculative prefetches, and retries: customers see either overcharges (speculative costs) or under-credits (no refund for failed fanout items). Goal: design and implement a consolidated metering model that provides deterministic, customer-facing billing that is correct for partial successes, retries, and fanout with shared resources (embeddings + rerank + toolchain).
acceptance_criteria: Metering event schema extended with per-stage provenance (request_id, idempotency_token, stage, provenance_id) and stored in ledger-db
Reconciler service produces deterministic correction events within 10 minutes of detecting a partial success pattern for >=95% of cases in test harness
Rate-limiter supports soft-reservation windows (configurable per-customer) and honors fairshare across concurrent fanouts
Billing pipeline consumes reconciler corrections and final invoiceable events match the reconciler output for a synthetic workload (integration test)
SDK requires idempotency token for non-chat structured endpoints and server returns clear guidance for missing tokens
End-to-end e2e test coverage for: full success, full failure, partial success (one of N tools fails), retried requests, and speculative prefetches
tasks: Design and publish metering-event schema (add provenance fields and stage enums)
Implement soft-reservation in rate limiter: reserve quota for request lifetime, release on timeout or reconciler correction
Build reconciler service: find partial success patterns, compute corrections, emit refund or charge events
Update billing ingestion so reconciler corrections override initial events; ensure idempotency of billing ops
Add SDK validation and client docs for idempotency_token on structured endpoints
Add integration tests in platform/integration-tests to simulate fanout patterns
Create dashboards: reconciler queue, reconciliation throughput, correction rate, customer-facing charge diffs
Canary rollout plan for reconciler and billing changes with per-tenant opt-in
discussion_notes: 2026-02-28 - Initial proposal: favor deterministic reconciler that prefers conservative refunds over speculative chargebacks to avoid customer surprise (Asha)
2026-03-02 - PM (Evelyn): High priority for customers with heavy rerank+toolchain workloads; asked for SLA on reconciliation latency

2026-03-04 - Design review: trade-off between immediate refund vs batched reconciler; decided on near-real-time reconciler (goal: <10min) with batched persistence windows to reduce DB write amplification (Marco)
2026-03-06 - Engineering: raised concern about scaling reconciler for high-fanout endpoints; proposal to use sampling and escalate on threshold breaches
2026-03-10 - Security: flagged need to avoid exposing internal provenance ids in customer-visible invoices (ops will map to opaque tokens)
2026-03-11 - Observability: suggested adding per-request fingerprint in trace logs to simplify manual investigations
design_decisions: Use idempotency_token as the canonical key for deduplication across retries and to tie speculative prefetches to parent requests
Implement per-stage provisional events: initial 'provisional' metering on reservation, final 'invoiceable' event after reconciliation
Refund policy: automated refunds for failed fanout items within 24 hours; manual review required for edge cases flagged by anomaly detectors
Conservative approach for partial success: refund only the explicit failed sub-item token cost, not the shared upstream rounding fees (documented in customer-facing billing docs)
qa_notes: Integration harness includes injected failures at tool boundaries and simulated network timeouts
Add deterministic replay mode to reconciler tests so CI can assert correction outputs consistently
Manual QA to validate invoices for 5 enterprise customers in staging before canary

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: reconciler can't keep up with peak fanout leading to delayed refunds -> Mitigation: start with sampling + high-priority queue for enterprise tenants

Risk: over-refunding due to race between reconciler and late success responses -> Mitigation: use final-idempotency-confirmation token and 5-minute settled window before issuing refunds for high-cost ops
Risk: billing divergence between old pipeline and new reconciler output -> Mitigation: run reconciler in shadow mode for 2 weeks and reconcile totals before toggling production path
customer_impact_summary: Customers running high-fanout embeddings + rerank + function-call pipelines currently report confusing charges when tool invocations partially fail. This work reduces overcharges and increases billing transparency by issuing deterministic corrections and clarifying SDK requirements. High-impact for enterprise customers with reserved capacity and those on tight quota windows.
